decisions.executionNote: Coin is left of center in this layout; use left arm only. Begin a raised, elbow-up approach with gradual downward wrist orientation.
Continue raised left-arm approach toward the visible holder, maintaining gradual wrist rotation and configuration continuity.
Advance above the holder while rotating toward a top-down pinch. Coin orientation will be refined from the closer wrist view.
Bring the left wrist above the coin, keeping clearance while completing the downward approach.
Complete the overhead alignment, then assess coin yaw and centering before descending.
Match the coin's visible plane with a small yaw adjustment and descend toward a centered pinch, keeping the jaws open.
The closer view shows the yaw correction needs the opposite sign. Align the coin edge vertically between the jaws while descending only 15 mm.
Fine-align the coin edge to the jaw midline and lower 5 mm for the pinch; keep the right arm parked.
Coin edge is centered between the jaws. Close the left gripper without moving, then verify retention with a small lift.
Allow the pinch to finish closing and begin a gentle vertical test lift; retention must be checked visually.
Lift the coin clear of the holder by over 8 cm while keeping the pinch closed and orientation fixed.
The coin is no longer visibly between the tips after lifting. Reopen and reassess above the holder rather than transport an unconfirmed grasp.
Reapproach the tilted coin with open jaws, correcting its lateral shift. Descend cautiously for a deeper pinch.
Center the tilted coin between the jaws and lower to its rim for a deeper, slower grasp attempt.
Close around the lower, tilted coin without translating. A slower subsequent lift will test whether this deeper pinch retains it.
Finish closing and settle the coin between the jaws before a very small test lift.
Lift slowly with the gripper held closed, watching for separation from the holder and coin motion relative to the tips.
Continue the slow vertical lift, keeping the pinch closed while the coin clears the holder.
The coin now remains visibly between the tips and is separating from the holder. Raise it further, still slowly, before transporting to the bank.
Coin remains retained. Begin carrying leftward toward the bank while raising for clearance above its slot.
Carry the retained coin toward the bank at safe height, keeping the coin plane fixed.
Continue toward the slot with the coin securely closed in the left gripper and clearance over the bank.
Move over the bank at constant height; slow down for wrist-camera slot alignment.
Slot is visible just beside the coin. Make small horizontal corrections at clearance height before insertion.
Align the slot centerline to the held coin with millimeter corrections and a small yaw adjustment while beginning a slow descent.
The coin and slot now have matching yaw; correct the small lateral overshoot and lower another centimeter while keeping the grasp closed.
Continue a slow vertical insertion approach with a final small lateral correction; monitor the slot around the coin edge.
Near the slot, reduce descent speed and refine the coin centerline by about two millimeters before releasing.
Pause descent and correct both the lateral and lengthwise alignment of the visible coin with the slot.
Slightly relieve possible rim contact and correct the lateral alignment in smaller increments; keep the coin clamped.
Coin is aligned over the slot. Lower six millimeters with a submillimeter centering correction, keeping the jaws closed.
The coin is centered on the slot at insertion height. Open the left gripper in place and observe whether it drops inside.
The released coin is still visible at the slot. Allow it to settle and lift the open jaws slightly without lateral disturbance.
The coin has disappeared into the slot. Withdraw the open left gripper upward and back before returning both arms to their starting poses.
Retract away from the bank while gradually restoring the left wrist orientation. Correct the small accumulated drift of the parked right arm.
Continue the smooth elbow-up return, moving back and lowering gradually with open jaws.
Lower toward the starting height while finishing the wrist recovery, maintaining joint-configuration continuity.
Approach the original poses with smaller coordinated translation and rotation increments; grippers remain open.
Finish the coordinated return to the initial end-effector poses, then check settling and episode status.
